recent_posts.title: Reimagining LinkedIn’s search tech stack
recent_posts.summary: LinkedIn rebuilt its search infrastructure using large language models to enable semantic search that understands natural language intent rather than just keyword matching. The system uses GPU-based embedding retrieval, small language model ranking with cross-encoders, and LLM-based query understanding to serve millions of queries per second. Key innovations include multi-teacher distillation for training compact models, context compression techniques (summarization and embedding compression) to reduce inference costs, and an LLM judge framework for continuous quality measurement aligned with product policy. The approach achieved double-digit improvements in search quality while maintaining inference costs comparable to traditional recommendation systems.

recent_posts.title: Building the next generation of job search at LinkedIn
recent_posts.summary: LinkedIn rebuilt their job search system using advanced AI to move beyond keyword-based search to natural language understanding. The new system uses large language models, embedding-based retrieval, and GPU infrastructure to understand complex job search queries like 'Find remote software engineer jobs in Silicon Valley with above median pay.' The architecture splits into retrieval and ranking stages, uses synthetic training data generation, and employs model distillation techniques to balance accuracy with computational efficiency at scale.

recent_posts.title: Liger-Kernel: Empowering an open source ecosystem of Triton Kernels for Efficient LLM Training
recent_posts.summary: Liger-Kernel is an open-sourced library designed to enhance GPU efficiency for training large language models (LLMs), offering 20% improved training throughput and 60% reduced memory usage with minimal code changes. Since its release in August 2024, it has gained significant traction and is integrated with major training frameworks like Hugging Face Trainer and PyTorch FSDP. Liger-Kernel uses efficient Triton-based kernels and offers multiple integration options to suit various customization needs. Benchmarks indicate substantial performance gains, making it a valuable tool for the ML community.

recent_posts.title: New Era of Transformation Brings a New Way of Thinking About Work
recent_posts.summary: The rapid advancement of AI, especially generative AI, is ushering in a new era of cognitive transformation, fundamentally changing business operations and the future of work. AI is not just enhancing processes but reinventing them, necessitating a shift in how tech stacks, skills, and team structures are approached. Employees will need to adapt by upskilling and developing soft skills to work effectively with AI. This transformation presents both challenges and opportunities, requiring comprehensive strategies and collaboration across industries to shape a future where human-AI collaboration thrives.

recent_posts.title: How data is powering skills-based hiring on LinkedIn
recent_posts.summary: LinkedIn is using data to power skills-based hiring through its feature called Skills Match. The feature connects job seekers and recruiters based on skills by comparing a candidate's profile with the job description. Skills Match prioritizes explicit skill signals and uses specific criteria to boost job skill quality. The threshold for a 'strong' skill match is set at approximately 10% of overall applications. The equitable impact of Skills Match is amplified through the integration of a Graph Neural Network (GNN) model, which improves hiring outcomes, relevance of search results, and brings benefits to underrepresented groups. LinkedIn is continuously working to enhance Skills Match and explore ways to incorporate member feedback and real-time GNN inference.

recent_posts.title: Matching LinkedIn members with the right Premium products
recent_posts.summary: LinkedIn Premium offers four products with distinct features and pricing to help professionals, job seekers, and small businesses stand out and gain insights for career development or business growth. Matching the ideal offering to each member is achieved through a unified machine learning platform that recommends the right product, creative, and channel based on member feedback and value proposition.

recent_posts.title: Responsible AI update: Testing how we measure bias in the U.S.
recent_posts.summary: LinkedIn provides an update on testing how they measure bias in AI systems in the U.S. They discuss the challenges of measuring algorithmic bias and the limited availability of race and ethnicity information. LinkedIn outlines their approach, which focuses on effectiveness, privacy, and member control. They have developed a privacy-preserving probabilistic race/ethnicity estimation system to achieve their goals.

recent_posts.title: Responsible AI update: Testing how we measure unfair bias in the U.S.
recent_posts.summary: LinkedIn provides an update on testing how to measure unfair bias in AI systems in the U.S. They outline the challenges and opportunities of measuring algorithmic bias and introduce their approach to measurement, focusing on comprehensive race and ethnicity demographic information while maintaining privacy and member control.

recent_posts.title: LakeChime: A Data Trigger Service for Modern Data Lakes
recent_posts.summary: LakeChime is a data trigger service that unifies data trigger semantics for modern and traditional table formats in data lakes. It supports both partition triggers and snapshot triggers, providing backward compatibility with Hive and forward compatibility with modern table formats. LakeChime enables simpler data lake migrations, incremental compute, and ease of integration with data producers, consumers, and scheduling systems. The key foundation of LakeChime's data trigger system is the Data Change Event (DCE), which captures data changes within a data table. Users can leverage LakeChime's partition and snapshot triggers to tailor their data processing workflows. Furthermore, LakeChime integrates with Airflow to facilitate efficient incremental processing with Spark on Iceberg tables.
